title: Zenith Solutions x Redwood Intro & Discovery

Header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Carter (Redwood AE); Ravi Singh (Redwood SE); Amira Patel (Zenith Head of Cloud Partnerships); Derek Ma (Zenith VP Infrastructure); Omar Reyes (Zenith GPU Sales); Taylor Ng (Zenith Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Intro, partnership models, technical compatibility, security checklist, pilot scope.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena Carter from Redwood Inference, AE on partner programs. Quick round robin?
[00:08] Amira: Hi I'm Amira, lead cloud partnerships at Zenith, thanks for setting this up.
[00:12] Derek: Derek here, VP infra, I'll be the technical counterpart.
[00:15] Omar: Omar, handle GPU partnerships and channel.
[00:18] Ravi: Hey all, Ravi from Redwood, I'm the solutions engineer, will dig into the integration details.
[00:25] Taylor: Taylor, security, quick questions on compliance.

[00:30] Lena: Great, agenda - quick intros, partner models (reseller/referral/marketplace), high-level tech fit, security, then identify next steps. Sound good?
[00:38] Amira: Sounds good. We're particularly curious about how Redwood would fit into our marketplace and whether we can resell dedicated capacity to our enterprise accounts.

[01:05] Ravi: Cool, quick high level - Redwood has three deployment modes: hosted API for self-serve, Dedicated reserved GPU capacity with SLA, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated customers. From a partner angle we support reseller listings, referral credits, and marketplace integrations - we have a partner program deck I can share.

[01:40] Derek: For us the requirements are predictable latency and data isolation. A lot of our customers are in finance/healthcare, so VPC or on-prem is a must. How mature is your private deployment?

[01:58] Lena: We recently shipped a Private control plane for enterprise - it's customer-managed networking, supports VPC peering and an on-prem package. We integrate KMS/HSM and provide audit logs. Implementation usually runs 6-12 weeks depending on access and compliance gates.

[02:20] Taylor: Are you SOC 2 and ISO certed? How about SSO and SAML for RBAC?

[02:28] Ravi: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. We support SAML/SSO for SSO integrations and role-based access controls. For keys we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. We'll share the security pack; expect some redactions but it has the major controls.

[02:50] Omar: From a go-to-market perspective - can we resell Redwood Dedicated as a packaged SKU? Like offer reserved pools and markup?

[02:58] Lena: Absolutely - reseller model is supported. Typically we do a partner contract with capacity commitments and enable quoting via our partner portal. Margins and deal registration can be discussed with partnerships/legal.

[03:22] Amira: We also want to understand the tech ops - how are updates and model rollouts handled for dedicated/private? Downtime?

[03:30] Ravi: Good Q - Dedicated runs an orchestrated runtime with canary rollouts, automatic fallback to previous model variants, and metrics. For Private deployments we coordinate upgrades, we expose rollout controls and we can schedule maintenance windows so you don't get surprises.

[03:55] Derek: For benchmarks - we need to validate latency at our target concurrency. Typical seq lengths vary, but we see 512 tokens for generation workloads and some shorter 128 token calls for chat. Can you support perf runs?

[04:10] Ravi: Yep. We recommend a joint benchmark: we'll run identical requests against Redwood Dedicated and a baseline (e.g., customer's current vendor) to compare p99 latency, median latency, throughput, and token cost. We'll share a template for workload profiles and a runbook.

[04:36] Lena: Do you have any constraints on data residency? Some of your customers asked for EU-only.

[04:44] Amira: Yes - must be able to restrict to EU regions. Also some require audit logs retained 1 year.

[04:52] Ravi: We can route regionally and provide audit logs retention options - that's configurable in the Private/Dedicated offering.

[05:10] Taylor: Slight note - any PII handling? Are you doing any telemetry? We need details for our DPO.

[05:18] Ravi: We'll include a section in the security pack about data handling/telemetry. By default we don't store request content for hosted customers beyond retention windows unless opted in; for Private you control retention and logs.

[05:40] Omar: On hardware - what GPU families do you support? We see customers asking for A100-class and some Ampere alternative. Also - any quantized/8-bit variants?

[05:52] Ravi: Our runtime supports modern NVIDIA families (A100, H100), and we have quantized execution paths. We also partner with select cloud GPU vendors for optimized kernels. We'll note specific performance profiles per model.

[06:12] Derek: Are there known model compatibility issues? For example large seq lengths and KV cache handling?

[06:20] Ravi: We support KV cache management and transparent batching. There are tunable knobs for cache eviction and shard placement. Occasionally model forks or custom layers need a small integration effort - we'll flag those during onboarding.

[06:40] Lena: From a commercial timeline - what does Zenith want? Pilot first or immediate marketplace listing?

[06:48] Amira: Pilot first. We want to validate latency/cost and then offer to a handful of customers via our marketplace.

[06:56] Lena: Makes sense. Proposed pilot: 4-6 week joint benchmark, then a short pilot with 2 customers. Target review at end of pilot to decide marketplace listing.

[07:10] Omar: Sounds good. Are there any legal/contract blockers we should know about? Data processor terms, liability caps?

[07:18] Lena: Standard partner contract covers data processing addenda (DPA), liability caps are negotiable at enterprise levels. We'll share an outline. Legal can handle deal registration and margin terms.

[07:36] Taylor: Will you provide pen test reports? We may need to run our own.

[07:42] Ravi: Yes, we can share pen test summaries; customers often do their own assessments. For Private/on-prem we cooperate closely on assessment windows.

[08:00] Amira: For the benchmark, typical metrics we want: p50/p95/p99 latencies, cost per 1k tokens, throughput at 99% SLA, and tail latencies at our concurrency.

[08:15] Ravi: Great - we'll map those into the template. Also curious on your expected QPS and concurrency - that drives the Dedicated pool sizing.

[08:25] Derek: For the pilot customers, typical QPS is 80-120 with spikes to 400 for batches. Concurrency often is 50-100. We'll send exact numbers.

[08:40] Lena: Quick note - we have intelligent batching and KV prefix caching that can significantly reduce cost for chat-style workloads. We'll include case studies in the deck.

[08:55] Amira: Are you able to integrate to our billing/marketplace APIs? We have a standard billing connector.

[09:03] Ravi: We have APIs for billing and usage export; work with partnerships to map marketplace SKUs. For white-labeled billing we can also support metering exports to your system.

[09:20] Omar: Any known competitors you see often in this space?

[09:25] Lena: Common ones are cloud vendors (AWS/GCP) and specialized infra providers like Paperspace or Lambda Labs; model-level vendors less so. We'll share competitive positioning.

[09:40] Derek: One more technical - how do you handle model rollbacks under load? We need deterministic fallback to previous versions.

[09:48] Ravi: We have canary traffic splitting and automatic rollback triggers based on error and latency thresholds. For Dedicated we also keep warm model variants to reduce cold-starts.

[10:05] Amira: Good. Let's talk logistics - timeline and immediate next steps.

[10:12] Lena: Proposed immediate next steps: 1) Send partner deck + security pack, 2) Redwood and Zenith agree on workload spec, 3) Redwood drafts benchmark template, 4) schedule technical deep dive with Derek/Ravi and engineering.

[10:28] Amira: That works. Also loop in our biz dev - I'll introduce our marketplace PM after the benchmark template is shared.

[10:36] Lena: Perfect. Any last-minute questions?

[10:40] Taylor: Just a security note - please include specifics around consent and data retention in the security pack, we need that for procurement.

[10:47] Ravi: Will do.

[10:50] Lena: Thanks all - we'll follow up with materials within a couple business days and target the technical deep dive for the week of July 13.

[10:58] Amira: Thanks, looking forward.
[11:00] Derek: Thanks everyone.
